examples.text: Tectonic plates move just a few centimeters per year — about as fast as your fingernail grows! Scientists measure this slow movement using GPS satellites.
Scientists use GPS and satellites to track the plates! They measure exactly how fast and in what direction they move.

There are three plate boundaries: convergent — plates collide and one subducts or land crunches up; divergent — plates move apart and new crust forms; transform — plates slide horizontally past each other with no crust created or destroyed.
At a divergent boundary, two plates pull apart! Magma rises from below, cools down, and forms brand new crust.

What happens when plates crash into each other?

At a convergent boundary, plates push and collide! This creates tall mountains, deep trenches, and lots of earthquakes and volcanoes.

At a transform boundary, plates slide and grind past each other sideways! This rough rubbing often causes strong earthquakes.
You can find the Philippine Trench on the eastern side of our country, right inside the Pacific Ocean!

Where can we find the Manila Trench?

It is found west of Luzon and Mindoro, right under the South China Sea!

On a Philippine map, label the Sierra Madre mountains in eastern Luzon, Mayon volcano in southeastern Luzon, the Philippine Fault crossing several islands, and the Philippine Trench east of the archipelago. Compare PHIVOLCS fault and trench maps with a topographic map. Look for patterns; nearby mountains and faults do not all mark separate major plate boundaries.
Did you know not all Philippine mountains are volcanoes? Some were just pushed up when giant earth plates crashed together, with zero volcanic activity!

Where does the Philippine Fault run?

It runs all the way from northern Luzon, passes through Leyte, and goes down to southern Mindanao!

The Philippine archipelago is made of several island arcs! Each has its own trenches and volcanoes, giving regions different features.

Real crustal blocks rotate and deform; coastlines change. Use measured Philippine Sea Plate velocities with their reference frame for a real estimate, and never treat the whole archipelago as one rigid plate or the sketch as a certain prediction.
At divergent ridges, new seafloor spreads outward at a slow but steady rate of about 2 to 20 centimeters per year.

Plates move over the deformable, mostly solid asthenosphere. Mantle flow and plate motion interact; avoid a picture of plates floating on a liquid ocean or riding a simple conveyor belt. Record the source and the model’s limits.

What lies beneath the lithosphere?

The asthenosphere! It is a hotter, softer part of the mantle where the tectonic plates above slowly slide.

Do tectonic plates float on liquid magma?

Tectonic plates do not float on liquid magma, but move over the solid yet plastically flowing rock layer called the asthenosphere!

What happens when one tectonic plate slides under another?

Deep ocean trenches form below, and volcanoes form above!

Why do the Philippine islands curve like a smile on the map?

They sit above a curved boundary where one plate dives under another. This curved row of volcanic islands is called an island arc!

An oceanic plate descends beneath an overriding plate at a subduction zone. Locked contact can build strain released in earthquakes. Water released from the descending slab lowers the melting temperature of parts of the mantle above it; magma can feed a volcanic arc. This is different from claiming the entire sinking plate simply melts.

What happens as the plate sinks at the Philippine Trench?

It produces earthquakes! These are the earthquakes that PHIVOLCS carefully monitors.

What happens when one tectonic plate slides under another?

Deep ocean trenches form below, and volcanoes form above!

How is the trench connected to our volcanoes?

As the plate sinks into Earth's hot interior, it melts into magma! This magma rises up to build volcanoes nearby.
When two plates push together, Earth's crust crumples and rises up — forming giant mountains like the Himalayas!
The Himalayas in Asia have the world's tallest peaks, including Mount Everest! They formed when India's plate crashed into Asia's plate — and they're still slowly rising today!

Compare a collision diagram of India and Eurasia forming the Himalayas with oceanic Nazca Plate subduction beneath South America at the Andes. Both involve convergence and crustal shortening, but the Andes also have a volcanic arc associated with subduction. A mountain’s height alone does not reveal its tectonic mechanism.
The Himalayas formed from two continents colliding! The Andes formed from an ocean plate sinking under a continent, so they grow differently.
When two giant pieces of Earth's crust called tectonic plates collide, the land gets pushed up to form mountains!

What happens when plates crash into each other?

At a convergent boundary, plates push and collide! This creates tall mountains, deep trenches, and lots of earthquakes and volcanoes.
Philippine coral reefs are in danger! Rising ocean temperatures and acidification from climate change are causing coral bleaching to happen more often and get worse.

How do scientists know Earth is warming up?

Scientists combined temperature measurements from around the world and found Earth's average temperature is rising—the warmest years on record happened in recent decades!

What happens because of the extra trapped heat?

Polar ice melts and sea levels rise!
Because the Earth is warming, large sheets of ice and glaciers at the poles and on mountains are melting!

What happens because of the extra trapped heat?

Polar ice melts and sea levels rise!
In parts of the Philippines, sea level has been rising faster than the global average!

How do scientists know Earth is warming up?

Scientists combined temperature measurements from around the world and found Earth's average temperature is rising—the warmest years on record happened in recent decades!
Too many greenhouse gases trap more heat, and the whole Earth slowly warms up!
Burning coal and fuel releases greenhouse gases that warm the planet and raise the sea!
When fossil fuels are burned, they release carbon dioxide! This gas causes pollution and global warming.

What happens when we burn fossil fuels?

Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide that warms the Earth!

During El Niño, the Philippines gets hotter and drier with less rain, so PAGASA watches closely for drought.
El Niño is a climate pattern from the Pacific Ocean that causes global weather changes all around the world!
La Niña is the cool phase of ENSO! It brings the Philippines more rain, stronger westward winds, and a higher risk of flooding.

How does La Nina affect the Philippines?

It brings extra rain, especially to the west, causing floods that can damage rice fields and buildings!
During El Niño, the Philippines gets hotter and drier with less rain, so PAGASA watches closely for drought.
El Niño is a climate pattern from the Pacific Ocean that causes global weather changes all around the world!
Stronger heat, floods, and droughts from climate change can damage crops and lower our food harvest!

Why is melting ice dangerous for the Philippines?

Greenhouse gases trap heat, melting huge ice sheets. This raises sea levels, which could flood our islands and coasts!

For a coastal community, preparing for flooding and protecting evacuation routes are adaptation to climate impacts. Reducing fossil-fuel use is mitigation because it lowers greenhouse-gas emissions. Compare local evidence and involve community planning: individual actions help, but effective protection also needs shared infrastructure and policy.
Planting trees helps fight global warming because they take in carbon dioxide straight from the air!
Gasoline vehicles release carbon dioxide! That's why walking, biking, or taking public transport really helps our Earth.
Using clean energy like solar and wind power releases fewer greenhouse gases!
We can lower carbon dioxide in the air! Just plant trees, use clean energy like solar power, and save electricity and fuel every day.
Using clean energy like solar and wind power releases fewer greenhouse gases!
Using clean energy from the sun, wind, and water helps cut down the carbon dioxide that warms our Earth!

How is the Philippines achieving a cleaner future?

By expanding renewable energy like solar, wind, geothermal, and hydroelectric to reduce greenhouse gas emissions!

Why is geothermal cleaner than a coal plant?

Coal plants burn fuel that runs out and makes lots of smoke! Geothermal burns nothing, just using Earth's heat, so it’s cleaner.

How is the Philippines achieving a cleaner future?

By expanding renewable energy like solar, wind, geothermal, and hydroelectric to reduce greenhouse gas emissions!

With no air resistance and level ground, a thrown object travels the farthest (greatest range) when launched at an angle of 45 degrees!

With a teacher, investigate a soft ball’s flight in a clear area. Hold release speed and height constant while varying angle; measure maximum height and horizontal range over repeated trials. Then keep angle fixed to compare speeds. The familiar 45° maximum-range result assumes no air resistance and equal release and landing heights; it is not a universal rule for basketball.

What decides how high a projectile goes?

Its upward launch speed! More upward velocity means a higher peak.

In an elastic collision, objects bounce apart without losing motion energy, so the total kinetic energy stays exactly the same before and after!
In an inelastic collision, objects stick together or get dented, turning some motion energy into heat and sound, but total momentum is still conserved!

A dart sticking into a dartboard is an inelastic collision because the dart and board stay together after impact.

A car crashing into a wall is an inelastic collision because the car deforms and much kinetic energy becomes sound and heat.

Compare a spring-bumper rebound with carts that stick. An ideal elastic collision conserves kinetic energy; an inelastic collision converts some into other forms. Check external forces before claiming total momentum is conserved.

Momentum is a cool measure of an object's motion! It is exactly equal to its mass multiplied by its velocity.
Inertia depends only on mass and exists at rest. Momentum is mass times velocity, so an object must be moving to have it!
Momentum is a cool measure of an object's motion! It is exactly equal to its mass multiplied by its velocity.
Momentum has a specific direction because it depends on velocity, which always points in the direction of motion!
A heavier moving object has more momentum at the same speed, making it harder to stop! That’s why a big truck is tougher to stop than a bicycle.
Why is a running elephant harder to stop than a tiny mouse? It's momentum! At the same speed, the elephant's huge mass gives it way more momentum.

A seatbelt holds you in place when a car suddenly stops, keeping you safe from flying forward!

How does a seatbelt keep you safe during a crash?

It stops your body from flying forward because of inertia, keeping you safe and secure!
An airbag makes your body stop more slowly during a crash, so the push on you feels much softer and safer!
In a crash, an airbag inflates fast to give your head and chest more time to stop, making the hitting force much smaller!
A crumple zone is the part of a car designed to crush and fold in a crash! This makes the impact take longer, lowering the force on passengers.
Crumple zones in cars extend collision time! Since impulse equals force times time, a longer collision means less force hits the passengers — keeping them safer!

What is a crumple zone?

Engineering sources say a crumple zone is a designed crush space in the front or rear! It’s not random damage, it helps the cabin decelerate over a longer time.

Almost all the electricity in our homes comes from large generators in power plants that are spun by turbines!

How does a power plant make electricity from coal?

Coal is burned to heat water into powerful steam! This steam spins a turbine, and the turbine generates electricity for our homes.

What happens to electricity at a substation?

At a substation, the high voltage is lowered before electricity is sent to homes in the area!
Transmission lines carry bare wires with very high voltage! They rely on the air and tall towers for safety instead of using insulation.
From the substation, electricity travels along poles on the street and right into our homes!

What happens to electricity at a substation?

At a substation, the high voltage is lowered before electricity is sent to homes in the area!
Your home's electric meter measures exactly how much electricity your family uses, counting it all up in kilowatt-hours!
The electric meter measures energy in kilowatt-hours (kWh)! One kWh means using a 1,000-watt appliance for one hour. Your electricity bill is based on the kWh you consume.
Always keep your hands dry when touching a plug or switch! Wet hands let electricity flow much more easily.
Never touch electric devices with wet hands! Electricity passes easily through water, which can be very dangerous.
When unplugging a device, always hold the plug, not the cord, so the wire stays safe and undamaged!
Overloading one extension cord with many appliances creates excess heat that can melt wires and start a house fire!

How do electric cars save energy when braking?

In electric cars, the motor can act as a generator when braking, so some energy is returned to the battery!
A motor and a generator are almost the same machine, but they work in reverse! One makes motion from electricity, and the other makes electricity from motion.

How do electric cars save energy when braking?

In electric cars, the motor can act as a generator when braking, so some energy is returned to the battery!
A motor and a generator are almost the same machine, but they work in reverse! One makes motion from electricity, and the other makes electricity from motion.

How do generators and motors work in the energy chain?

A generator changes mechanical energy into electrical energy! A motor changes it back. They are opposite steps in the exact same cycle!
On a sunny day it is better to use daylight than to switch on lights, to save electricity!
We help the environment and save money when we simply turn off the lights and appliances we are not using!

How can you easily save electricity at home?

Simply turning off lights you are not using saves electricity!
Give your home plenty of shade and good airflow! This naturally reduces the need for air conditioning and electricity.
Save electricity by turning off unused lights, unplugging full chargers, and setting the aircon to 25°C or higher. Small steps lower your bill!
Geothermal energy releases far less carbon dioxide than coal plants! While coal causes air pollution and climate change with its emissions, geothermal uses Earth's renewable heat with minimal impact.

Coal plants burn fuel that runs out and makes lots of smoke! Geothermal burns nothing, just using Earth's heat, so it’s cleaner.
A hydroelectric plant burns no fuel or coal, so it gives off no smoke or air pollution while it makes electricity!
Large hydropower dams can impact the environment — they may block fish migration, change downstream water temperature, and displace communities from flooded areas.

Roasting Pili nuts in Bicol causes a chemical change that permanently alters their color and flavor!
Fruit ripening and rotting, like in a banana, are chemical changes! You can see it when the color, taste, and smell change.
Signs of a chemical reaction include a color change, release of gas or bubbles, formation of a precipitate, and a temperature change!

How do the amazing stalactites in Sagada's Sumaging Cave form?

They form through a chemical change! Dissolved minerals in water precipitate and slowly turn into solid rock.
When you mix vinegar and baking soda, bubbling gas forms! This change cannot be undone.
Mixing vinegar and baking soda is a chemical change! Watch it fizz and give off carbon dioxide gas.
In an endothermic reaction, the thermometer reading drops because the reaction absorbs heat!
Sinangag is rice fried in hot oil with garlic! The heat browns them, creating yummy new smells and flavors.
Sinangag is rice fried in hot oil with garlic! The heat browns them, creating yummy new smells and flavors.
Fruit ripening and rotting, like in a banana, are chemical changes! You can see it when the color, taste, and smell change.
Milk is slightly acidic, with a pH of about 6.5.
Household ammonia is a base! It has a pH of about 11.

In a synthesis or combination reaction, two or more substances join to form a single new compound. For example, hydrogen and oxygen form water!
In a combination or synthesis reaction, two or more substances join together to form a single new product, like hydrogen and oxygen forming water!
In a decomposition reaction, a single substance breaks down into two or more simpler substances, which is often caused by heat or electricity!
In a decomposition reaction, one compound breaks apart into simpler substances! For example, electricity can split water into hydrogen and oxygen.

What happens in a single replacement reaction?

A more reactive element takes the place of another in a compound, like iron displacing copper!
When metal reacts with acid, it's a single replacement reaction! The metal replaces hydrogen, producing hydrogen gas and a salt.

What happens in a double replacement reaction?

Two compounds exchange their parts, called ions, to form two new compounds, and it often produces a solid precipitate!
Double replacement reactions happen when they form a solid precipitate, a gas, or water! This removes ions from the solution.
When fuel like wood or gasoline burns, it uses up oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide!

What happens when we burn fossil fuels?

Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide that warms the Earth!
Metal pickling uses acid (usually hydrochloric acid) to remove rust and surface scale from metal before painting! The acid reacts with and dissolves the iron oxide.

Can acidic foods like vinegar damage metal containers?

Yes! Acidic foods like vinegar, calamansi, and tomatoes can slowly corrode metals — so don't store them for long in unprotected metal containers!
When soaked in vinegar, the acid reacts with the shell's calcium carbonate. It releases carbon dioxide bubbles until the hard shell dissolves!

How does acid rain affect limestone and marble?

It reacts with calcium carbonate to dissolve them! This erodes marble buildings and creates karst caves over centuries, like in Palawan.

How do scientists write a formula equation for a precipitate reaction?

They write Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2 + 2KNO3!

How do we read a chemical equation?

Reactants go on the left of the arrow, and products on the right! The arrow simply means 'yields' or 'becomes.'
In a chemical equation, reactants are the starting substances before a reaction. Products are the new substances formed after, and they are separated by an arrow!

How do we read a chemical equation?

Reactants go on the left of the arrow, and products on the right! The arrow simply means 'yields' or 'becomes.'
In a chemical equation, reactants are the starting substances before a reaction. Products are the new substances formed after, and they are separated by an arrow!
In a chemical change, atoms aren't destroyed! They just rearrange to form new substances, keeping the total amount of matter the same.
In any chemical reaction, the number of each kind of atom is the same before and after! The total mass does not change, only the arrangement does.
Burning wood doesn't destroy matter! The original mass is conserved in the remaining ash and released gases.
Antoine Lavoisier gave us the Law of Conservation of Mass! It says mass is never created or destroyed during a chemical reaction.
To see conservation of mass when a reaction makes gas, the container must be sealed! If it is open, the gas escapes and the weight seems to drop.
In a closed system, total mass stays the same before and after a chemical reaction! Matter isn't created or destroyed, it just changes form.
We balance a chemical equation by adding coefficients! This makes sure the number of each atom is exactly the same on the reactant and product sides.

Change coefficients, never subscripts: replacing H2O by H2O2 would change water into another substance. This is a written model, not an experiment to ignite gases.
We balance a chemical equation by adding coefficients! This makes sure the number of each atom is exactly the same on the reactant and product sides.
A chemical equation is balanced when each type of atom has the same number on both sides, since atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction!

Change coefficients, never subscripts: replacing H2O by H2O2 would change water into another substance. This is a written model, not an experiment to ignite gases.
To check if an equation is balanced, count each element's atoms! Just multiply the coefficient by the subscript in each formula.
Food spoils faster in air because oxygen helps microbes break it down! That’s why we seal food in cans or airtight bags to keep it fresh longer.
Frozen food lasts longer than fridge food because the deep cold pauses bacteria! It doesn't kill them, just stops them from moving and multiplying.

What does insulin do after eating?

After eating, the pancreas releases insulin to help cells take in glucose from the blood. In diabetes, this doesn't work properly, so blood sugar stays too high.

Natural selection changes the whole population over many generations — not a single individual.

What is Charles Darwin known for?

Charles Darwin is famous for the theory of evolution by natural selection.
Bacteria become resistant to antibiotics through mutation, the survivors reproduce and pass on their resistance, slowly creating stronger superbugs.

What does 'survival of the fittest' mean?

In Darwin's theory, 'survival of the fittest' means animals best suited to their environment survive and reproduce!

Use a reliable biology textbook as a secondary source. Natural selection occurs when inherited differences affect survival and reproduction in an environment. Can an animal choose to adapt?

No! Adaptations aren't a choice — they appear through variation and selection across many generations.
Genetic variation in a population fuels natural selection — traits that help survival are more likely passed on to the next generation.

What is an adaptation?

An adaptation is an inherited trait that helps survival in a certain environment — it builds up over many generations because natural selection favors helpful traits.

What is natural selection?

In natural selection, animals with traits that fit their environment survive and have young more often, so more offspring inherit that helpful trait over time.

Why does the Philippines have so many endemic species?

Because our islands separated from each other over millions of years — this isolation is why so many endemic animals and plants evolved here!
Only traits passed down through genes can shape a population's future—that's the key to how natural selection works over time.

What is biotechnology?

Biotechnology uses living things like bacteria, yeast, and plants to make useful stuff — like food, medicine, and even fuel!

What's a bioreactor used for?

A bioreactor is a large industrial tank used to grow microorganisms at a huge scale, making products like antibiotics and insulin.

How does bagoong stay preserved so long?

Small fish or shrimp are mixed with lots of salt and left to ferment — microbes and salt keep it from spoiling while deepening its flavor!
Yeast isn't the only fermenter — bacteria sour food too, like in yogurt and buro, while yeast makes alcohol and gas.

Not all mold is bad — some kinds are actually used to make certain types of cheese!
Yogurt, cheese, and bagoong are all made with help from tiny microbes, in a process called fermentation.
The soy sauce (toyo) we pour on our food is made from soybeans broken down by a special mold called koji, which gives it its distinct flavor.

How does tuba turn into coconut vinegar?

Bacteria ferment the coconut sap tuba, converting alcohol into acetic acid!

Is nata de coco made of coconut meat?

No! Nata de coco is not chopped coconut meat — bacteria build it from coconut water, so it's really more like clear jelly.

Where does nata de coco come from?

Bacteria actually make it! They ferment coconut water and build up a thick, edible mat of cellulose — that becomes the chewy nata de coco.

How does Bt corn fight off caterpillars?

Bt corn is a GMO with an added gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, making it produce a protein that kills caterpillars that eat it — so less pesticide is needed.

How much food a place has limits how many animals can actually live there!
Carrying capacity isn't one fixed number, it changes depending on the food, weather, and condition of a place.
The size of a population is held in check by factors like food and water shortage, disease, competition, and predators.

In a logistic model, population growth slows near carrying capacity as resources become limiting. Food, water and shelter affect how many organisms can be supported; access to mates also affects reproduction. Carrying capacity changes with conditions, and real populations may fluctuate or overshoot rather than settle at a perfectly fixed number.
